chapter: Brother Remus and the brass bands
title: Brother Remus and the Lindsey string band
summary: Remus's start on drums with the Lindsey family string orchestra at penny parties.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: Yeah. I saw him. I wondered about you a little more about your brothers. About Remus now. He was the oldest. Do you know, did he have any lessons or when did he start? Did he ever tell you, of course he was older than you, but did he ever tell you when he started on drums, how big he was? My brother?
Yes. No, he never did tell me. When I was big enough to know, I was going to dance and he was playing with Penny Poets.
And who did he play with?

Whose bands? Well at that time, that's a fellow that you don't know anything about, and very few people talk about that. His first bunch, I remember good, I was in these pants, used to wear bloomer pants. They said, they're playing with Old Man Lindsey now. Old Man Lindsey. Old Man Lindsey. Old Man Lindsey had a string orchestra in the family. Horven Lindsey, and Old Man Lindsey, and Johnny Lindsey. You see? Then they add on. They had a fan on my brother. I remember that good. And they add on this brother they call, Dude, split clarinet.

No, Gabriel. I mean, which brother played with him? Bebe. Bebe. Bebe. Or Remus, my brother Remus, the oldest brother, he never did worry about trap drum. They used to be bass drum and snare drum. On the street post, right? He's the one you put in. He's the one you put in. He's the one you put in. Bass drum and snare drum. He was good at both of them. So that's why when I first seen my brother play trap drum, it was with Old Man Lindsey playing. He played a penny party. See? And he had Dude on clarinet. Johnny Lindsey on bass. That's Johnny's instrument. And Herbert Lindsey on violin. Well, they both died. Now Herbert, both of them died in Chicago. Yeah. And he went and he kept on going big then. And him and when I played again, I was big enough to go around then, you see. So he made me help him through third district fair to bring his drums. I went with him several times, but that first time he went to third district fair to go by the economy hall. And he climbed to my hall and I stayed there all night, see. And they made me play something there with Old Man, Marion Parade's name, see. That's the break me and Buddy Johnson, all of us was from Algeist. And Jimmy Pala, see he was from Algeist too, he was leading the band there. He was from Algeist. That was before Pete was leading. Pete used to lead the superior band too. But Jimmy was before Pete, see. And Jimmy used to play alto, toot-toot horn in the brass band and violin in the orchestra. All musicians was doubling up on the streets and this. They didn't like now, they just take one or two numbers and say they know everything. It wasn't like that in the damn days. He was trying to learn something.
